content: 1. Post-marketing cases have demonstrated QT prolongation in patients who overdosed on voriconazole, particularly when combined with other illnesses or drugs that cause electrolyte imbalances or prolong QT intervals. 2. Both voriconazole and quinine increase the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor patients closely. 3. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of quizartinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 4. When quizartinib is co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, reduce the dose to 4 mg/day or interrupt quizartinib for the duration of strong CYP3A inhibitor use. 5. Voriconazole and ranolazine both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 6. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of repaglinide by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 7. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 8. Voriconazole increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. No rilpivirine dose adjustment is required. 9. Rilpivirine increases voriconazole toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor patients. 10. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 11. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of ripretinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 12. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 13. Voriconazole and risperidone both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 14. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of roflumilast by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 15. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of roflumilast topical by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 16. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 17. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 18. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Adjust the dosage of CYP2C19 substrates if clinically indicated. 19. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of saxagliptin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 20. When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce saxagliptin to 5 mg/day. 21. Voriconazole increases the levels of seladelpar by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 22. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers taking seladelpar and co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 23. Selpercatinib increases voriconazole toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. 24. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of selpercatinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 25. Sertraline and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 26. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 27. Voriconazole and sodium sulfate/potassium chloride/magnesium sulfate/polyethylene glycol both decrease serum potassium levels. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 28. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 29. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 30. Sorafenib and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 31. Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 32. Sparsentan decreases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 33. Sparsentan, a CYP2C19 inducer, reduces the exposure and efficacy of CYP2C19 substrates. 34. Stiripentol and voriconazole interact by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 35. Stiripentol is both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. 36. Stiripentol increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 37. Consider reducing the dose of CYP2C19 substrates if adverse reactions occur when co-administered with stiripentol. 38. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 39. Co-administration of sufentanil SL with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 40. Sulfamethoxazole and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 41. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 42. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 43. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus ointment by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 44. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 45. Voriconazole and tamoxifen interact by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 46. Voriconazole and tamoxifen interact by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 47. CYP3A4 inhibition decreases the metabolism of tamoxifen to N-desmethyl tamoxifen, an active metabolite with similar biological activity. 48. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tasimelteon by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 49. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of voriconazole by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 50. Tecovirimat increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 51. Tecovirimat is a weak inhibitor of CYP2C8 and CYP2C19. 52. Tecovirimat decreases voriconazole levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 53. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 54. Telavancin and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 55. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 56. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. 57. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 58. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 59. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 60. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 61. Thioridazine and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 62. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tiagabine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 63. Voriconazole increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 64. Ticagrelor is metabolized by CYP3A4/5. Avoid use with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 65. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 66. Voriconazole increases levels of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 67. Tisotumab vedotin’s active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE systemic exposure and the risk of adverse effects. 68. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 69. Voriconazole increases levels of toremifene by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 70. Toremifene metabolism may be inhibited by drugs known to inhibit CYP3A4 hepatic enzymes. 71. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of tramadol by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 72. Trazodone and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 73. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 74. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 75. Triclabendazole and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. 76. Triclabendazole increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 77. If plasma concentrations of CYP2C19 substrates are elevated during triclabendazole use, recheck plasma concentrations after discontinuation of triclabendazole. 78. Trifluoperazine and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 79. Trimethoprim and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 80. Trimipramine and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. 81. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 82. Triptorelin increases voriconazole toxicity via QTc interval prolongation. Use caution and monitor patients. 83. Triptorelin increases the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 84. Tropisetron and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 85. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of ulipristal by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 86. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 87. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate; co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 88. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of upadacitinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 89. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 90. Valbenazine and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 91. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 92. Reduce vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day; do not exceed 200 mg/day if weight >50 kg. 93. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 94. Vardenafil dose may need to be reduced if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 95. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of velpatasvir by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 96. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 97. Venlafaxine and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 98. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 99. Voriconazole increases verapamil levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 100. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 101. Fluticasone furoate and vilanterol are both CYP3A4 substrates; co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 102. Voriconazole increases levels of vinblastine by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 103. Voriconazole increases levels of vincristine by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 104. Voriconazole increases levels of vincristine liposomal by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor patients. 105. Voriconazole and voclosporin both increase the QTc interval. 106. Voriconazole and voclosporin both increase the toxicity of the other via nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 107. Co-administration with drugs associated with nephrotoxicity may increase the risk for acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity. 108. Vorinostat and voriconazole both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients. 109. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of warfarin by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 110. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 111. Reduce zanubrutinib (a CYP3A4 substrate) to 80 mg once daily if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Interrupt dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous zanubrutinib dose. 112. Voriconazole and ziprasidone both increase the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 113. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 114. Reduce zuranolone dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 115. Acetazolamide increases voriconazole levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 116. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 117. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of aliskiren by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown.
